title: Dose-dependent myelin g-ratio alterations in the white matter of 16p11.2 copy number variations
abstract: Copy number variations (CNVs) at the 16p11.2 locus are major genetic risk factors for neurodevelopmental conditions and drive reciprocal alterations in cerebral white matter structure and connectivity. However, whether these alterations reflect differences in the axonal or myelin compartments remains unresolved with conventional diffusion MRI. We combined diffusion MRI with magnetization transfer saturation mapping across two ComBat-harmonized cohorts comprising 80 controls, 26 16p11.2 deletion carriers, and 13 duplication carriers. We quantified axonal volume, myelin volume, and aggregate g-ratio of white matter tracts forming the structural connectome. Metrics were evaluated using normative modeling across tract length, resting-state functional networks, and cortical nodes. We additionally examined 29 individuals carrying other neurodevelopmental CNVs. 16p11.2 gene dosage was associated with regional reciprocal differences in tract axonal volume, with greater volume in deletion carriers and lower volume in duplication carriers. In contrast, myelin volume did not differ significantly from controls. This mismatch resulted in pervasive aggregate g-ratio alterations, with higher g-ratios (relatively thinner myelin sheaths) in deletion carriers and lower g-ratios (relatively thicker sheaths) in duplication carriers. Regional g-ratio alterations also extended to other neurodevelopmental CNVs. These findings resolve some of the biological ambiguity underlying white matter alterations in 16p11.2 CNV carriers, implicating the axonal compartment while revealing comparatively stable myelin volume. The disrupted axon-myelin scaling results in connectome-wide g-ratio alterations and may represent a shared microstructural hallmark of genetic neurodevelopmental risk.

title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
abstract: Purpose: To test whether a daytime nap was associated with improved associative-recognition performance relative to monitored wakefulness and to determine where any response-time (RT) difference occurred in the RT distribution. Methods: Fifteen healthy students completed nap and wake sessions in a within-participant design. Each session included word-pair learning, immediate recognition, a 60-min interval, and delayed recognition without additional study. Trial-level log RT was the focal outcome; accuracy and electroencephalography (EEG) were complementary outcomes. Results: The RT Condition-by-Time interaction was significant (b = -0.063, 95% CI [-0.117, -0.009], p = .027). Responses were 6.7% faster after the nap (p = .010) but did not change after wakefulness (p = .704), with the difference concentrated among slower responses. Accuracy showed no condition-specific change (p = .401). Nap EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger periodic sigma activity, but no EEG measure explained the RT effect. Conclusions: Daytime napping was associated with faster delayed associative recognition, primarily through attenuation of the slowest responses. The exploratory findings warrant larger confirmatory studies.

title: Activity-gated exocytosis drives myelin remodeling required for adult learning
abstract: Myelin remodeling is emerging as a dynamic facet of plasticity in the adult brain. Learning and sensory experience induce remodeling of existing myelin sheaths through incompletely understood mechanisms, leaving its causal contribution to adaptive behaviors unclear. Here, we identify activity-dependent exocytosis in mature oligodendrocytes as a key driver of myelin remodeling. Live-cell imaging reveals that neuronal activity stimulates oligodendrocyte exocytosis. Exocytosis in mature oligodendrocytes drives myelin sheath elongation on optogenetically stimulated axons in adult mice. Disrupting exocytosis in pre-existing myelin, but not newly formed myelin, impairs motor skill acquisition, suggesting that remodeling of pre-existing myelin sheaths is required for learning. These results uncover a cellular mechanism that couples neuronal activity to myelin membrane remodeling and provide a molecular handle to interrogate the function of myelin plasticity across different circuits, behaviors, and neurological disorders.

title: Inverse covariation between the neocortex and the limbic system is concentrated at deep evolutionary divergences
abstract: The macroscale architecture of mammalian brains consists of a broadly conserved set of structures, but the relative sizes of these structures vary substantially across species. Much of this variation follows conserved scaling relationships, but particular systems can expand or contract relative to the rest of the brain, providing targets for adaptive selection. One prominent example is a volumetric tradeoff between the neocortex and the limbic system, in which expansion of one is associated with reduction of the other, a feature apparent when brain structure volumes are examined across living species. However, whether this relationship has operated throughout mammalian evolution or arose during particular periods of diversification is unknown. Using phylogenetic comparative methods, we here show that the tradeoff between the neocortex and the limbic system is concentrated at deep evolutionary divergences separating major mammalian groups. After accounting for shared ancestry and brain size, the tradeoff strengthens progressively among deeper branches of the mammalian phylogeny, extending broadly across limbic structures, with the strongest signal involving olfactory components. Recent divergences show no consistent relationship. Our analyses indicate that the neocortex-limbic tradeoff emerged during the early diversification of mammals, highlighting how present-day variation in brain organization retains signatures of ancient evolutionary transitions.

title: The marginal brain
abstract: Goal-directed cognition raises brain energy use only a few percent above resting use, a figure often read as evidence that cognition is metabolically cheap. Models of endogenous precision derive the precision of neural representations from a cost on encoding activity whose unit price is a free parameter. Embedding endogenous precision in a regulated, shared energy budget makes this cost the shadow price of energy at the margin of the budget. Neither the task share of the budget nor the net whole-brain increment identifies this price; when tasks face a common price ratio and coding technology is stable, imprecision changes by the exact fourth root of that ratio, so that the cost of information rescales while its shape is preserved; and the co-movement of imprecision and stimulus-linked task energy separates price changes from changes in coding technology. In 12,960 published estimation trials, response variance at matched numerosities rises with prior width in line with the ratios that the calibrated model predicts out of sample, and simulations indicate that a doubled price is detectable with existing paradigms when state-dependent lapses are modeled.

title: The limbic navigation system as a hierarchical RNN
abstract: Path-integration-trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can reproduce grid-like and head-direction-like representations, but most existing models rely on low-dimensional velocity inputs and do not capture the hierarchical organisation of the brain's self-localisation circuit. We introduce a hierarchical recurrent neural network (HRNN) that separately processes angular velocity and linear speed to perform simultaneous angular and positional path integration. Trained on these tasks, the HRNN generalises to longer timescales than seen during training and develops neural response properties resembling all the key cell types: angular velocity cells, head direction cells, speed cells, conjunctive and pure grid cells. The learned circuit also recovers key motifs of the navigation system, including attractor dynamics and asymmetric connectivity patterns. Perturbation analyses reveal functional information flow across the hierarchy, consistent with experimental observations. Finally, introducing theta-paced mutual inhibition between two learned angular-velocity subpopulations enables the HRNN to reproduce the bidirectional theta sweeps observed in empirical data. These results establish hierarchical task-driven RNNs as a biologically interpretable framework for linking neural representations, circuit motifs, and population dynamics in spatial navigation, while enabling targeted in silico perturbations and the generation of experimentally testable predictions.

title: Generalized prefrontal task-progress sequences efficiently encode task structure
abstract: The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) occupies a central role in executive function including decision-making, rule learning and cognitive flexibility. Here, we investigated how mPFC populations represent the animal's progression along sequential task stages. Freely moving mice performed an odour-guided two-choice task requiring sensory sampling, action selection, navigation, and reward collection. Population activity in the mPFC formed sequences that evolved through cue sampling, movement towards the reward sites, and reward-related epochs. These sequences exhibited a shared temporal organization across trial types, pointing to a generalized encoding of task progress by prefrontal neurons. Artificial neural networks trained on the same task developed task-progress sequences, and experimentally disrupting task-progress tuning in these networks impaired learning efficiency. Our results indicate that mPFC activity organizes behavioural episodes along correlated trajectories and suggest that task-progress tuning offers an efficient solution for the encoding of task space during multi-stage behaviour.

title: Left Temporoparietal Neural Synchrony Tracks Cooperative Performance Across Adult Dyads
abstract: Cooperation requires interacting individuals to coordinate their actions toward shared goals, and interpersonal neural synchrony (INS) has been proposed as a neural correlate of this coordination. However, the relationship between INS and cooperative performance remains heterogeneous, and relatively little is known about how it varies across social relationships. The present study examined INS and behavioral performance during a naturalistic cooperative tabletop Jenga task in close-friend, romantic-partner, and mother--child dyads (N = 284 participants). Brain activity was simultaneously recorded using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) hyperscanning, and INS was quantified using wavelet transform coherence across the bilateral inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) and temporoparietal junction (TPJ). Cooperative performance was assessed using tower collapse and the number of valid turns completed during the game. True interacting dyads exhibited significantly greater neural synchrony than surrogate dyads across all examined regional pairings (d range = 0.35-0.55), indicating robust interaction-related inter-brain synchrony. Behavioral performance was not associated with INS at the whole-network level. Region-specific analyses, however, showed that tower collapse was associated with reduced synchrony in the left TPJ-left TPJ (p Bonf = 0.009) and left TPJ-right TPJ (p Bonf = 0.017) pairings, whereas the number of valid turns was unrelated to INS. Follow-up analyses further indicated that the association between tower collapse and left TPJ--left TPJ synchrony was present in close-friend (p Bonf = 0.020) and romantic-partner (p Bonf = 0.026) dyads but not in mother-child dyads. These findings suggest that the behavioral relevance of interpersonal neural synchrony is not uniform, but depends on the neural systems involved, the specific index of cooperative performance, and the relational and developmental context in which interaction unfolds.

title: Social brain fingerprinting: unique functional connectomes underpin interpersonal behaviours in non-autistic and autistic adults
abstract: Human social interaction requires continuous adaptation while preserving stable individual patterns of brain organisation. This study examined whether functional connectome fingerprinting captures person-specific organisation during reciprocal interaction and whether its spatial architecture relates to social role and autistic traits. fMRI data from 70 adults forming 35 dyads were analysed during an iterated Ultimatum Game: 19 non-autistic Proposer-non-autistic Responder dyads and 16 non-autistic Proposer-autistic Responder dyads. Functional connectivity across 400 cortical parcels was used to assess whole-brain identifiability and edge-wise reliability. Connectomes remained identifiable across datasets, roles, and task conditions, with no reduction in global identifiability in mixed dyads. Edge-wise analyses revealed role-related and dataset-dependent differences across distributed large-scale networks. Role-sensitive connectivity features were associated with Autism-Spectrum Quotient scores, supported out-of-sample prediction, and topology-derived features classified AQ-threshold status above chance. Stable connectomic signatures therefore persist during reciprocal interaction while their network organisation varies with social role and autistic traits.

title: Sleep reactivation shapes memories of event and its temporal structure
abstract: Episodic memory provides a temporal scaffold that organizes past experiences according to their sequential occurrence. While memories are reactivated and consolidated during sleep, it remains unknown how exogenous reactivation reshapes memories of complex events, particularly the temporal structure that binds individual elements across time. In this preregistered study, 35 participants encoded neutral and aversive narratives composed of image sequences, with auditory context shifts defining event boundaries. During post-encoding slow-wave sleep, closed-loop targeted memory reactivation (TMR) delivered boundary-associated auditory cues time-locked to the up-state of slow oscillations. Reactivation led to faster, more confident, and more liberal recognition responses for cued than uncued memories. However, reactivation exerted a time-dependent effect on temporal-order memory, impairing it immediately after sleep but attenuating forgetting one week later. This behavioral dissociation was paralleled at the neural level: stronger cue-elicited theta activity predicted superior recognition of neutral, but not aversive event content, whereas greater theta responses were associated with poorer temporal-order memory for the same events. Together, these findings suggest that sleep reactivation does not uniformly strengthen episodic memories. Rather, it selectively prioritizes access to event content while reorganizing temporal relations among event elements, revealing distinct, time-dependent consequences of sleep reactivation for different components of complex experiences.

title: The human hippocampus retroactively binds experiences across time
abstract: Creating memories requires linking events across seconds and minutes, but canonical mechanisms of associative plasticity operate over much shorter timescales. This poses a fundamental problem: how can the brain bind information that arrives at different times? Computational model and animal studies implicate the hippocampus in associating events across time, but when the hippocampus becomes engaged and how it interacts with representations of preceding events are unknown. Here we show, using intracranial recordings in humans forming image-word associations across a ~2-s temporal gap, that hippocampal high-frequency activity predicts later memory when the second event arrives, but not during the initial image or intervening delay. At this moment, neurons tuned to the preceding image reinstate stimulus-specific firing despite its sensory absence. Across trials, hippocampal high-frequency activity was selectively coupled to this reinstatement during successful encoding and increased before spiking of image-tuned neurons. These findings reveal a retroactive mode of hippocampal binding, whereby representations of preceding events are recruited when new information arrives. This mechanism provides a neural solution for binding experiences across the temporal discontinuities that characterize everyday life.

title: Polyglutamine-expanded TBP rewires neuronal and muscle proteomes beyond transcription in a Drosophila model of SCA17
abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 17 (SCA17) is an age-related neurodegenerative disorder caused by polyglutamine expansion in the TATA-binding protein (TBP). TBP is a core transcription factor, but pathogenic polyglutamine expansion likely rewires cellular programs beyond transcription. Here, we utilized Drosophila strains that express wild-type (WT) or pathogenic (SCA17) TBP in neurons or skeletal muscle, which we analyzed vs. controls via TMT mass spectrometry, profiling of eight post-translational modifications, and RNA-seq. Shared TBP-WT and TBP-SCA17 responses predominated, impacting ribosomes and mitochondria while repressing innate immunity. Disease-specific effects were narrower and tissue-dependent: SCA17 activated xenobiotic, retinoid, and glutathione-redox pathways in the CNS, but attenuated anabolism in muscle compared to TBP-WT. Many proteomic changes occurred independently of mRNA changes, implicating post-transcriptional mechanisms. Knockdown of select SCA17-regulated proteins reduced cytotoxicity, validating omics-identified modifiers of SCA17 pathology. These findings distinguish shared TBP dosage effects from disease-linked, tissue-specific polyglutamine responses and identify evolutionarily conserved targets for SCA17.

title: Differential Survival of Retinal Ganglion Cell Types Following Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion
abstract: Background. Branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) is a common cause of retinal ischemia, rapidly inducing neuronal death and often producing irreversible vison loss. Interventions such as thrombolysis restore perfusion but cannot recover neurons already lost, and most patients retain permanent visual deficits. Identifying which neuronal populations die, and how rapidly, may therefore reveal timing windows and targets for neuroprotective treatment. Aims. To determine the timing of pathology, we evaluated vascular changes and neuronal degeneration in a photocoagulation-induced mouse model of BRVO. To determine differences in retinal ganglion cells (RGC) type susceptibility, we tracked the survival of RGC subpopulations using immunofluorescence markers. Methods. BRVO was induced by retro-orbital injection of Rose Bengal and FITC dextran followed by targeted photocoagulation of a branch vein. Obstruction was confirmed by fluorescein angiography and vascular damage was viewed by optical coherence tomography angiography. Cell survival was quantified by immunostaining at 3, 7, and 14 days using RNA Binding Protein with Multiple Splicing (RBPMS, pan RGC). RGC subtype markers for intrinsically photosensitive RGCs (TBR2),  RGCs (SPP1), ON OFF direction-selective RGCs (CART), and F RGCs (FOXP2) were used to examine differences in survival across RGC types. Results. Occlusion selectively disrupted the superficial and intermediate capillary plexus, sparing the deep plexuses. All examined neuronal populations were significantly depleted, but with markedly different magnitude and timing.  RGCs and F RGCs were the most vulnerable subtypes, both approaching complete loss by one week, whereas intrinsically photosensitive RGCs were the most resistant. Conclusion.  RGCs, typically resilient in glaucoma, trauma, and excitotoxicity, were markedly vulnerable in BRVO, indicating that RGC subtype susceptibility is insult-specific.

title: A brain immune phenotype independent of Alzheimer's Disease associates with amyloid susceptibility and systemic inflammation
abstract: Transcriptomic and proteomic studies have consistently demonstrated substantial molecular heterogeneity across patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other neurodegenerative disorders, leading to the proposal of multiple disease subtypes. However, almost all previous studies have focused on heterogeneity within diseased cohorts, whereas comparatively little attention has been paid to the molecular diversity of neurologically healthy individuals. In the present study, we demonstrate that one of the most prominent transcriptomic programs characterized by a strong immune component previously interpreted as an AD-specific immune subtype is in fact a brain phenotype that exists independently of AD yet interacts with AD susceptibility and is selectively associated with amyloid pathology. The transcriptional effect of the immune phenotype exceeds that of AD pathology-induced changes and is accompanied by alterations of brain cellular compositions and a distinct systemic inflammation. Our findings suggest that part of the molecular heterogeneity observed in neurological diseases might arise from pre-existing brain phenotypes rather than representing disease-specific subtypes. These insights support a precision medicine approach for Alzheimer's disease, whereby individuals with an immune phenotype of the brain could be prospectively identified and monitored, enabling the application of targeted preventive strategies before substantial neuropathology and cognitive decline emerge.

abstract: Preterm survivors often develop motor and socio-cognitive impairments that implicate altered cerebellar development, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. A key challenge is that prematurity involves overlapping perinatal insults that converge on the developing brain, making their individual effects difficult to disentangle. Here, we model two major prematurity-associated insults, maternal immune activation (MIA) and neonatal hypoxia (Hx), in mice. By controlling timing and sequence, we define how these insults shape cerebellar assembly during rapid maturation. Comparative analysis with human tissue confirmed that these insults recapitulate key features of the human preterm cerebellum, establishing the translational validity of this model for dissecting insult-specific outcomes. Behavioral and kinematic profiling revealed divergent motor and social phenotypes, which we traced to insult-specific cerebellar remodelling. Hypoxia compromised both granule cell maturation in the internal granule layer and the principal excitatory afferents to Purkinje cells, a circuit state that manifested as impaired motor execution and stereotyped, sensory-disengaged social investigation. Maternal immune activation, by contrast, expanded the granule cell progenitor layer and reduced Purkinje cell dendritic complexity, a phenotype that preserved social preference but reorganized the kinematic structure of social investigation. When hypoxia followed maternal immune activation, it acted on this primed substrate to produce a distinct state in which the features established by prior inflammation were compounded by granule cell proliferative arrest, progressive mitochondrial dysfunction, and aberrant, hyper-interactive social investigation. Together, these findings reframe prematurity-associated insults as cerebellar reprogramming events shaped by both the identity and sequence of insults, linking distinct mechanistic substrates to divergent neurodevelopmental outcomes.

abstract: Synaptic dysfunction is among the earliest pathological events in Alzheimer's disease and among the strongest neuropathological correlates of cognitive impairment, yet blood-based synaptic biomarkers are lacking. Whether serum β-synuclein provides prognostic information independent of established amyloid-β (A; CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio) and tau (T1; CSF pTau181) biomarkers has not been determined. We studied 259 non-demented individuals with subjective or mild cognitive impairment from a single-centre memory clinic, classified by CSF biomarkers using externally validated cut-offs into A-T1- controls (n = 97), A-T1+ PASSED ('pTau and Aβ surge with subtle deterioration', n = 65), and A + T1+ Alzheimer's disease (n = 97), with parallel analyses using Aβ40-normalised pTau181. Endpoints comprised dementia conversion (n = 185, median follow-up 4.1 years), all-cause mortality (n = 258, median 7.0 years), longitudinal MMSE trajectories (n = 185), and regional brain volumes (n = 137). Independence from CSF biomarkers was quantified through systematic effect attenuation analysis. Serum β-synuclein was selectively elevated in the Alzheimer's disease group (Cohen's d = 0.69 vs controls, P < 0.001) but not in PASSED individuals (P = 0.40), and was more strongly associated with CSF pTau181 (r = 0.36) than with the Aβ42/Aβ40 ratio (r = -0.20) across the cohort. Each standard deviation increase was associated with higher risk of dementia conversion (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.11, 1.77; P = 0.005), faster cognitive decline (-0.11 SD/year, 95% CI: -0.18, -0.04, P = 0.002, corresponding to -0.20 MMSE points/year), and higher mortality (HR = 1.33; 95% CI: 1.07, 1.65; P = 0.010). For dementia conversion and mortality, adjustment for continuous CSF pTau181 and Aβ42/Aβ40 produced minimal attenuation (≤13%). Both associations were preserved under Aβ40-normalised T1 staging but not against continuous pTau181 normalised to CSF Aβ40. For cognitive decline, β-synuclein's effect remained significant after Aβ42/Aβ40 adjustment (25% attenuation; P = 0.007) but was substantially attenuated by pTau181 (58.5%; P = 0.186). Serum β-synuclein was associated with lower bilateral temporal lobe volume-the only lobar regions to survive hierarchical testing-with sub-regional involvement spanning the hippocampi, entorhinal cortex and parahippocampal gyrus, and explained 5.0-8.9% of unique variance beyond CSF biomarkers. Plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) showed a strong association with β-synuclein, estimated in the PASSED subgroup (β=0.34 per SD, P < 0.001). Serum β-synuclein provided prognostic information largely independent of CSF Aβ42/Aβ40 across all endpoints and of pTau181 for survival outcomes, while sharing substantial prognostic variance with pTau181 for cognitive trajectory, supporting its candidacy as a blood-based synaptic complement to core Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.

abstract: Ferroptosis is implicated in multiple human diseases, but the lack of bioavailable inducers has limited its physiological study and therapeutic translation. Here, we report KY0418, a selective covalent inhibitor of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) featuring an isourea warhead, with high plasma stability and broad tissue distribution after oral dosing in mice. KY0418 specifically targets GPX4 SeCys46 to induce ferroptosis hallmarks in human and mouse cancer cell lines, with greater selectivity than existing inhibitors. In a standardizable acute-liver-injury mouse model, KY0418 triggers ferroptotic ultrastructural changes matching those of established inducers, and systemic administration remodels tissue metabolism and generates hydroxyl radicals detectable by a chemiluminescent probe. Subcutaneous tumors from different cancers exhibited variable responses to KY0418 treatment, from no effect to about 70% growth inhibition, but KY0418 consistently eradicated circulating tumor cells and suppressed metastasis across multiple cancer models. These findings position KY0418 as a tool for advancing in vivo ferroptosis research and its clinical translation.

abstract: Efficient integration of gene-length cargos in vivo remains challenging. Non-long terminal repeat (non-LTR) retrotransposons, which naturally mobilize large DNA segments through an RNA intermediate, could potentially address these limitations. Here, we developed a computational pipeline to systematically identify a diverse set of non-LTR retrotransposons. Extensive engineering generated elements capable of the efficient and stable insertion of reporter genes in human cells using RNA templates introduced in trans, which we term Gene Writers. Gene Writers successfully generated CD19 and CD20 chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cells ex vivo with robust antitumor activity. Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNA delivery enabled in vivo CAR-T cell generation and stable B cell depletion in a humanized mouse model. Our study delineates a comprehensive framework for the discovery, engineering, and application of non-LTR retrotransposons and demonstrates their utility for gene-sized cargo delivery in vivo, thereby bridging a critical gap in existing gene therapy modalities.

abstract: T cell exhaustion limits the success of cancer immunotherapies, yet the proteomic changes underlying this dysfunctional state remain poorly understood. We integrated transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, turnover proteomics, and ubiquitin proteomics to construct a multi-omic atlas of T cell exhaustion. These studies identified pathways regulated through transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, including degradative and nondegradative ubiquitin modifications, and uncovered widespread changes in proteostasis, metabolism, and DNA repair. Major shifts were revealed in the ubiquitin-proteasome system, as differential expression of E3 ubiquitin ligases correlates with immunotherapy outcomes. These findings position the collapse of proteostasis as a central, underappreciated feature of T cell exhaustion and reveal opportunities to restore T cell function. We demonstrate that overexpression of the E3 ligase RNF166 enhances T cell persistence in vitro and in vivo. This work defines proteome-turnover dynamics as a critical regulatory layer in progressive T cell dysfunction, with broad implications for advancing cancer immunotherapy through manipulation of E3 ligases.

abstract: Brain development and function are influenced by the choroid plexus, whose dynamic cellular and transcriptional changes shape immune cell trafficking and cerebrospinal fluid composition. Here, we performed a comprehensive multi-omics analysis-including bulk and single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics-of the lateral ventricle choroid plexus across postnatal and adult stages in mice and rats. We identified changes in the choroid plexus cellular composition and gene expression profiles, including early and progressive activation of several immune related genes in main cell types from early postnatal to young adult stage. Epithelial cells exhibited developmental remodeling over time, characterized by distinct gene expression programs, locus-specific changes in chromatin accessibility, and cellular diversity. In addition, we uncovered an epithelial cell population characterized by a distinct transcriptional signature. Our study offers a comprehensive atlas of transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in choroid plexus cells, providing a valuable resource to guide future research.

abstract: In a delayed alternation spatial working memory task, hippocampal time cells fire during specific moments of the delay period to form a sequential representation of the entire delay interval. The causal relationship between these sequences and working memory remains unclear. Similarly, hippocampal theta oscillations are thought to support working memory, primarily through the generation of time cell sequences. To causally examine these relationships, we optogenetically silence the medial septal GABAergic theta-generating circuit during the delay portion of a delayed spatial alternation task. With hippocampal theta oscillations substantially reduced, many time cells exhibit remapping, and new time cells are recruited. Despite partial remapping of time cell sequences, behavioral performance remains intact and trajectory-specific coding is preserved, suggesting that task-relevant information remains available under theta disruption.

abstract: The retrosplenial cortex (RSP) supports spatial cognition, memory, and brain-wide information integration, yet its output architecture remains poorly resolved at single-neuron resolution. Using fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography (fMOST), we reconstruct sparsely labeled neurons sampled predominantly from the anterior RSP across the whole brain. We find three major projection routes-cortical-restricted (CR), thalamic-restricted (TR), and thalamic-brainstem collateral (TBC)-and classify neurons into ten projection subtypes with distinct target-selective profiles. Somatic location and volumetric features are associated with axonal projection patterns. TR-pattern neurons show subregion-dependent thalamic targeting, whereas TBC-pattern neurons display greater axonal complexity and subtype-specific collateralization toward thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain targets. Bilaterally projecting neurons across distinct projection patterns show cross-network projection modes with an overall ipsilateral preference and laminar-specific commissural architectures. Together, these findings provide a single-neuron anatomical map of RSP cortical, thalamic, and cortico-subcortical output patterns and a framework for examining distributed information processing across brain-wide networks.

abstract: Nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) regulates inflammation and immunity and is frequently dysregulated in autoimmune diseases, inflammatory disorders, and cancers. Cytokines and pathogens activate NF-κB transcription factors, and nutrients and metabolites, including fatty acids, also modulate its activation, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we report that RelA (p65), a major component of the NF-κB transcription complex, is autopalmitoylated at cysteine 197 and 206. Palmitoylation of p65 enhances its nuclear localization and p65-p50 complex formation, thereby increasing NF-κB transcriptional activities. We further show that licochalcone D, a small-molecule anti-inflammatory compound, directly inhibits RelA/p65 autopalmitoylation, suggesting it may act through an additional mechanism. These results indicate that fatty acid metabolism can directly regulate NF-κB activity through p65 palmitoylation and suggest that targeting p65 autopalmitoylation may be a therapeutic strategy for diseases with dysregulated NF-κB signaling.

abstract: Coleoid cephalopods, such as octopus, squid, and cuttlefish, have evolved remarkably large nervous systems with neuron numbers comparable to those of small mammals. Despite this, little is known about how these nervous systems develop, which genetic programs drive the formation and diversification of their neural cells, and what factors contribute to evolutionary brain expansion. This study combined single-cell multi-omics with spatial expression analysis to uncover the cell types and the regulatory mechanisms underlying nervous system development and evolution in Octopus vulgaris. We discovered an early embryonic glial cell population that is distinct from neurogenic progenitors and defined by orphan nuclear receptor 4a (nr4a), distal-less homeobox (dlx), and prospero homeobox (pros) regulons. Their spatial distribution and dynamic transcriptional profile during embryogenesis indicated that these cells might orchestrate cell migration, axon guidance, and brain patterning before expressing neuronal markers or differentiating into mature glia. Comparison of embryonic glial transcriptional signatures across two cephalopods, a gastropod, and Drosophila revealed shared expression of nr4a, dlx, and pros in mollusks, while embryonic glia in Drosophila expressed pros, dlx, repo, ttk, and gcm but not nr4a. Intriguingly, the overall gene expression profile of cephalopod embryonic glia has diverged from that of Pomacea canaliculata (golden apple snail), whose glia do not express guidance or patterning genes. Together, these findings identified a conserved embryonic glial cell type in mollusks that might have acquired new functions in coleoid cephalopods to organize neuronal migration and wiring in their expanded brain.

abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is the most common reactive chemical threat organisms face. Here, we map the neural circuit that drives chemotactic escape from environmental H 2 O 2 in the nematode C. elegans. Twenty-four neuron classes with sensory endings at the mouth and nose respond to H 2 O 2 , with dynamics encoding stimulus intensity and exposure history. Sensing begins when H 2 O 2 oxidizes the peroxidatic and resolving cysteines of the cytosolic peroxiredoxin PRDX-2, which relays this oxidative signal to cysteines on the LITE-1 and GUR-3 ion channels, triggering calcium influx in sensory neurons that drive escape. Most of these neurons release glutamate to drive H 2 O 2 -dependent excitation of AIA interneurons, whereas others signal through non-glutamatergic routes. Thus, the C. elegans nervous system monitors H 2 O 2 -induced changes in the intracellular H 2 O 2 -detoxification machinery and relays them to interneurons driving organism-wide escape. This raises the possibility that changes in neuronal activity in aging and neurodegenerative diseases arise from altered peroxiredoxin-mediated H 2 O 2 signaling rather than primarily from direct macromolecular damage by H 2 O 2 .

abstract: In this review, the first in a three-part series, we consider the origins of confounding in fMRI. We review the signal properties of an fMRI experiment and the intended sensitivity to neurovascular coupling, the hemodynamic response function, and the spatial-temporal biases imposed by the heterogeneous anatomy of the vascular system. We then explore the various mechanisms that can leave nuisance signals, often termed physiologic noise, in fMRI data. All mechanisms having a biological dependence are considered, including mechanical effects from head motion and respiration, blood gases, brain motion from the cardiac pressure wave, blood pressure, and scanner instabilities that couple with the participant's body.

abstract: Visual search is facilitated when targets reappear within invariant distractor layouts (contextual cueing). Although contextual cueing can bias attention within 150 msec, it remains unclear whether this guidance relies on global spatial configuration or requires object identity. We recorded ERPs while participants searched for targets in repeated versus novel arrays. Critically, each trial began with a placeholder display that conveyed only spatial configuration, preceding the search display by 500 msec. Following learning, targets were relocated and swapped their locations with a distractor in the opposite visual field, such that the overall search layouts remained unchanged. ERPs time-locked to placeholder onset revealed an early poster contralateral negativity (N1pc, 140-160 msec) for repeated contexts, despite the absence of target-specific object information. After relocation, this effect reversed polarity, indicating persistent orienting to the learned target location. A second N1pc, followed by N2pc and CDA, emerged only after search onset. These findings show that learned spatial structure rapidly guides attention, whereas effective selection requires additional processing of object information.

abstract: Neuroimmunology is a field of neurology focused on the diagnosis and treatment of diseases where the immune system causes inflammation or injury to the nervous system. This includes diseases such as multiple sclerosis, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, autoimmune encephalitis, autoimmune ataxia, stiff person syndrome spectrum disorder, and neuro-rheumatologic diseases such as neuropsychiatric lupus. Over the past couple decades, there have been significant advancements in the diagnostic methods for several neuroimmunologic diseases. Despite these achievements, major needs remain for additional methods to facilitate earlier diagnosis, monitor disease activity and treatment, and elucidate disease mechanisms to aid in the development of novel or tailored treatment strategies. Currently, there is often a trade-off between the invasiveness of neurodiagnostic testing and the level of detail that can be obtained from the test without causing an iatrogenic injury. Here, we discuss the potential of extracellular vesicles (EVs), especially CNS-derived EVs obtained from peripheral blood, as a promising avenue for advancing research and clinical care in neuroimmunology. This article provides a review of the key clinical features and approaches to care for the most common neuroimmunologic diseases. We identify gaps that remain in our current understanding of these conditions. We then highlight how ongoing research in the EV field may address these existing gaps. Finally, we examine the challenges that must be overcome before EV analysis can be more widely adopted in both research and clinical care in this field.

abstract: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes . Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes ; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies , we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51 + and CD51 − astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51 + and CD51 − astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51 + astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51 + astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51 + astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species , yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans . Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

abstract: The insular cortex has a central role in pain , interoception and feelings , yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal–posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral–posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior–polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress . Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health . However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light–electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

abstract: Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A , a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase . The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain . Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a -null mice and in human neurons . Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome.

abstract: Programming biological function—designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks—is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited : they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein–text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks—a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein—and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO 2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells . However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

abstract: Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored . Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

abstract: Wearable computing promises to transform human interaction with information, yet conventional graphical user interfaces (GUIs) rely on planar, rigid displays incompatible with textiles, which are composed of one-dimensional fibres. Despite recent progress in flexible and fibre-based displays, bridging this fundamental dimensional mismatch remains challenging because existing approaches do not naturally provide the digitally addressable, high-throughput, information-rich interfaces required for interactive GUIs. Here we present a digital pixel fibre integrating addressable pixels, a common propagation-axis interconnection for scalable in-fibre circuitry and a coaxial sensing layer for fibre-level touch localization. Microelectronic components and a touch-gated resistive path system form a linear circuit that acts as both an interactive display backbone and a computational bus, while peripheral multimodal fibre sensors and actuators enable physiological, inertial, optical, and acoustic input and output. We integrate these fibres into the forearm portion of a garment sleeve to realize a GUI with a 96 × 54-pixel display, 30-frame-per-second refresh rate and 8-bit colour depth. It supports dynamic graphics, integrated audio–video playback, wireless data exchange and interactive computing functions, while maintaining the flexibility, washability, breathability and mechanical robustness of everyday textiles. By merging display, sensing and computation within a single fibre, this work establishes a scalable platform for intrinsically interactive textiles, opening pathways toward garments that operate as fully integrated computational systems.

abstract: Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak yet critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for pleiotropic endogenous hormones. Here, we develop a peptide-centric, dose-resolved strategy, the two-dimensional peptide-centric local stability assay (2D-PELSA), which enables highly reliable target identification and direct estimation of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. Dose-dependent information converts static proteolysis signatures into quantitative readouts of local structural remodeling at enhanced resolution, resolving direct engagement, allosteric regulation, complex remodeling, etc. Applied to 17β-estradiol (E2)-treated BT474 breast cancer cell lysates, 2D-PELSA identifies 1288 conformotypic E2-responsive peptides and 24 candidate targets enriched in unsaturated and long-chain fatty acid metabolism with micromolar EC50 values. GPX4 is identified as an E2-engaged ferroptosis regulator with an EC50 of 2.4 μM and is downregulated by micromolar E2. Orthogonal Western blot and MS-based assays validate this interaction in lysates and living cells. Integrated proteomic, lipidomic and phenotypic analyses show that chronic micromolar E2 exposure induces lipid metabolic reprogramming, lipid peroxidation and oxidative, iron-dependent cell death that is only partially rescued by ferrostatin-1 or deferoxamine. These findings establish 2D-PELSA as a versatile platform for dissecting ligand-induced structural responses and mapping target landscapes in complex biological contexts.

abstract: The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

abstract: Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. Here, we introduce a scalable method to adapt Cell Painting for 3D spheroids. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. By profiling 52 clinically relevant drugs, we show that single-cell fingerprints clustered by biological pathway and resolved drug effects more robustly than those of flattened spheroid-wide views. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

abstract: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and organize into plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation modulates junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel–channel organization remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs containing multiple channels and determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two configurations. The interfaces lack extensive protein–protein contacts and instead contain ordered lipid densities that define much of the inter-channel interface. These interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting how channel organization may promote lipid occupancy near the pore. We also refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å, providing an internal reference and chemical detail of the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define lipid-rich interfaces as a feature of multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function.

abstract: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins ( e.g . XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi.

abstract: The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm.

abstract: Maternal caregiving requires sensory vigilance to ensure offspring survival, particularly during sleep. Infant cries are salient sensory cues that reliably trigger maternal arousal and caregiving responses in both humans and dams, but the underlying neural circuitry remains poorly defined. Here we identify a corticohypothalamic circuit in mice that mediates maternal awakening in response to pup calls. We show that layer 6 (L6) neurons in the temporal association cortex and ectorhinal cortex (TeA/Ect) projecting to the preoptic area (POA) exhibit enhanced responsiveness to pup calls after the transition to motherhood. This enhanced responsiveness is mediated by increased expression of dopamine receptor D1 (Drd1) in TeA/Ect → POA neurons. Additionally, we reveal a pathway from the auditory thalamus to L6 TeA/Ect neurons that transmits pup cues during sleep. Together, these findings identify a dedicated neural circuit that grants infant cries privileged access to arousal systems, likely representing a fundamental adaptation for caregiving across mammals.

abstract: Synaptic NMDA-type glutamate receptors (NMDARs) are central components of all neural computations. NMDAR levels critically vary between synapses but how the synaptic localization of NMDARs is controlled remains unclear. Here we show that SIK3, a serine–threonine protein kinase, localizes to synapses where it phosphorylates the obligatory NMDAR subunit GluN1 at a single site. This single phosphorylation event controls NMDAR recruitment to synapses. Genetic deletion of SIK3 severely and selectively decreases synaptic GluN1 levels by ~60% without altering AMPA-type glutamate receptor levels or inducing major transcriptional changes. Pharmacological inhibition of SIK3 impairs synaptic NMDAR responses within 45 minutes. Mutating the SIK3-phosphorylation site inhibits GluN1 synaptic recruitment. ‘Sleepy’, a gain-of-function mutation in SIK3 that increases sleep, selectively enhances synaptic NMDAR levels by increasing GluN1 phosphorylation. Thus, SIK3 phosphorylation of GluN1 provides a key signal for recruiting NMDARs to synapses.

abstract: Social disconnection is a major risk factor for anxiety disorders, the most prevalent mental illnesses worldwide, yet its neural substrates remain unclear. Here, we establish a comparative social deficit (CSD) model in adult male mice that induces a paradoxical phenotype of increased anxiety-like behavior together with heightened social preference, a pattern conceptually similar to human loneliness. Mechanistically, CSD increases the excitability of medial preoptic GABAergic (mPOA Gad2 ) neurons, which bidirectionally regulate CSD-induced behavioral changes. Transcriptomic and electrophysiological analyses identify downregulation of the Kv4.3 potassium channel (Kcnd3) as a molecular driver of mPOA Gad2 hyperexcitability. Furthermore, mPOA Gad2 neurons exert monosynaptic inhibition onto dorsal raphe serotonergic (DRN 5-HT ) neurons. This inhibitory projection, strengthened by CSD, mediates CSD-induced behavioral effects. These findings define a molecular and circuit mechanism by which social disconnection remodels mPOA-DRN interactions to drive the paradoxical coupling of anxiety and elevated social preference, providing a translational framework for understanding loneliness-related psychiatric vulnerability.

abstract: This study investigated Alu methylation levels in 85 ischemic stroke patients and 50 healthy controls, using Alu-Combined Bisulfite Restriction Analysis (COBRA) a quantitative approach to assess methylation. Ischemic stroke patients had significantly lower overall Alu methylation as compared to controls (P < 0.0001). Alu methylation was negatively correlated with age in both the control group (r = -0.6131, P < 0.0001) and the ischemic stroke group (r = -0.2834, P = 0.0086). Moreover, among age-matched ischemic stroke patients, there remained a difference between control and ischemic stroke patients (P = 0.0182). Alu methylation remained associated with ischemic stroke status after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR = 0.841, 95% CI = 0.709-0.979, P = 0.0327). Within the ischemic stroke group, disease duration was not significantly correlated with Alu methylation in the unadjusted analysis (r = -0.1594, P = 0.1450). However, after adjustment for age and sex, longer disease duration was associated with lower Alu methylation (β = -0.556, 95% CI = -0.994 to -0.117, P = 0.0137). Alu methylation was lower in patients with a history of multiple stroke events (P = 0.0323) and in those with Fazekas scores of 2-3 (P = 0.0324) in the unadjusted comparisons, but neither association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age and sex (P = 0.0542 and P = 0.0684, respectively). Stroke circulation location was not associated with Alu methylation. These findings support an association between Alu methylation and ischemic stroke status. Longer disease duration was also associated with lower Alu methylation after adjustment for age and sex. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish causality, disease progression, or predictive or prognostic value. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine the clinical relevance of these findings.

abstract: Hearing loss has been identified as a modifiable risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia, although most of the evidence is derived from studies in older adults. Identifying such cognitive impairment in midlife is crucial, as it serves as a baseline for understanding changes in cognitive abilities that occur later in life. The present study aimed to compare the cognitive performance of age- and socioeconomic status-matched middle-aged adults with normal hearing and those with untreated hearing loss. This study included 48 participants aged 40-65 years, comprising 24 adults with normal hearing and 24 with untreated hearing loss. Among the latter participants, 9 had unilateral loss and 15 had bilateral loss. The cognitive evaluation involved assessing memory (forward and backward digit span and contextual memory test), attention via the Go/No-Go task, and executive function via the letter and category fluency tasks. Results showed that adults with untreated hearing loss performed significantly poorer on all the cognitive tasks compared to their normal-hearing counterparts. Large effect sizes were observed for memory tasks, the category fluency task and Go/No-Go accuracy, and a moderate effect size for the letter fluency tasks. Furthermore, multivariate linear regression analysis demonstrated that better-ear pure-tone thresholds independently predicted cognitive performance, but not age or education. These findings provide preliminary evidence on the association between untreated hearing loss and cognitive performance in middle age. However, considering the modest sample size and cross-sectional study design, longitudinal studies are needed to determine the temporal relationship between hearing loss and cognitive changes.

abstract: Real-world distractors occur in environments whose states change at different rates. We asked whether such volatility alters initial overt oculomotor allocation, later target verification and response commitment, or both. Observers performed an additional-singleton search task with concurrent eye tracking while distractor presence followed high- or low-volatility sequences, with overall distractor prevalence held constant. Trial-pooled oculomotor capture was higher under high volatility, a pattern that appears to indicate altered filtering. Matching the same-location run position removed that difference, with no detectable difference in capture across volatility regimes at matched run position. The pooled capture effect was therefore consistent with a structural consequence of the volatility manipulation, which enriched high-volatility blocks with early-run positions where capture is intrinsically high. The volatility effect itself appeared on distractor-absent trials. Under high volatility, response times were longer, fixations more frequent, final-target dwell longer, and errors fewer, while target-acquisition latency itself was unchanged. Same-location repetition learning showed no detectable difference in slope across regimes. A hierarchical drift-diffusion model (DDM) and a complementary volatility Kalman-filter (VKF) comparison converged in showing that manual responses carried both boundary-related and drift-related structure. With distractor frequency held constant, the per-trial effect of volatility therefore emerged after the first saccade as an increase in response caution rather than in oculomotor capture. This pattern is consistent with precision-weighted adjustment to environmental uncertainty.

abstract: Background Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (FASD) arising from prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) are the leading preventable cause of neurobehavioral disorders. Early pregnancy is particularly vulnerable to ethanol toxicity, yet alcohol use often continues until pregnancy recognition. In Finland, national incidence estimates of PAE and FASD remain limited. Objective To estimate the incidence of any PAE and heavy PAE in Finland between 1990 and 2025, and to model the annual number of children with FASD born in Finland. Methods We developed a mathematical modelling framework integrating studies on alcohol use during pregnancy in Finland, biomarker-based estimates of heavy PAE, national population statistics, and international active case ascertainment studies on FASD prevalence. Incidence of any PAE was estimated from self-reported alcohol use, including pre-recognition exposure. Heavy PAE was estimated by combining binge-drinking prevalence, delayed pregnancy recognition, biomarker data and anonymous self-reports. FASD incidence was modelled using two approaches: 1) an international multiplier linking FASD prevalence to heavy episodic drinking prevalence among women (Model M), and 2) a conventional epidemiological ratio between any PAE and FASD (Model L). Results Self-reported alcohol use during pregnancy declined following abstinence recommendations in the early 2000s, while pre-recognition use remained relatively stable. Heavy PAE decreased from 9% (uncertainty range 7-11%) in the 1990s to 6% (4-8%) in the early 2020s. Any PAE declined from 75% (60-85%) to 32% (26-38%). Modelled FASD incidence showed similar decreasing trends, ranging from 6.8% to 5.6% (Model M), and from 6% to 3% (Model L). Conclusion PAE remains common in Finland, and the burden of FASD is substantial despite declining trends. Additional biomarker-based studies of PAE and active case ascertainment of FASD are needed to refine current estimates. Strengthened public health efforts to reduce PAE, including the efforts before recognition of pregnancy, are essential.

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have evolved from relying primarily on knowledge stored in their parametric memory to using non-parametric memory mechanisms such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide and ground knowledge. Recently, LLMs have begun to perform retrieval autonomously within a reasoning loop, an approach referred to as Agentic RAG. This shift introduces new querying behaviours, with implications for the design of retrieval systems that have yet to be evaluated. In this work, we introduce a large-scale dataset (ASQ) capturing how Agentic RAG systems perform multi-step search and reasoning. ASQ contains about 1M agentic search traces collected from open-source Agentic RAG systems over 3 corpora, 5 agent variants, and 6 retrieval settings. Our analysis of ASQ shows that, within this controlled benchmark setting, a single search query can trigger long chains of retrieval calls (up to 186) and follow query reformulation dynamics different from those observed in historical human-search data. Our results also reveal substantial behavioural variation across agent and retrieval configurations: changes in re-ranking and retrieval depth do not consistently affect search workloads in terms of search-call volume and trace length across agents. To our knowledge, publicly available production logs do not expose the agent, dataset, and retrieval configuration associated with each trace. ASQ provides a reusable resource for further analysing agent search behaviour and supporting future information retrieval studies on agentic workloads under controlled settings.

abstract: Previous work demonstrated that ectodermal cells exhibit greater susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 than endodermal and mesodermal cells, raising concerns about potential vulnerability of the developing nervous system. We hypothesized that neural stem cells (NSCs) derived from human ectoderm are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2. Using pseudotyped viral particles representing both wild-type and Omicron spike variants, we confirmed efficient transduction in NSCs, with Omicron variants preferentially utilizing endocytosis-mediated entry. Inhibition of endocytosis with filipin and OcTMAB significantly reduced viral entry across all spike variants. Low glycosylation levels on NSCs facilitated viral entry, and enzymatic removal of glycosylation increased their susceptibility. Ectodermal infection by SARS-CoV-2 raises serious concern for potential teratogenic effects on the nervous system, possibly causing latent or subclinical anomalies not immediately evident at birth. Therefore, future clinical studies and long-term surveillance of infants and children exposed in utero are necessary to investigate and identify potential neurodevelopmental deficits.

abstract: The successor representation (SR) is a reinforcement learning strategy which has been suggested to underlie nuanced forms of habitual behavior, rendering it a candidate mechanism for mental health conditions thought to involve habitual control, such as addiction. However, paradigms used to assess habits in humans cannot detect SR use. Together with the fact that they are usually conducted in disorder-irrelevant contexts, this may explain why the evidence for a hypothesized shift from goal-directed to habitual behavior in addiction is inconsistent. Here, we tested whether individuals with high-risk (n = 260) compared to low-risk drinking behavior (n = 260) rely more on SR or a rigid goal-based dimension-reduced SR variant, particularly in alcohol-related contexts. An online multi-stage decision-making task performed in either a virtual bar or apartment context allowed us to dissociate (red)SR from model-based and model-free learning strategies by testing how well participants adapted their choices to different types of distal changes in the environment. Findings suggest that a particular type of SR, namely a (reduced) random-policy SR-like strategy, contributes to human behavior, but that high-risk drinkers do not differ from low-risk drinkers in their use of this strategy. Instead, both groups seem to rely less on what is likely a (reduced) random-policy SR strategy in alcohol-related contexts - and instead more on model-free control. Results suggest that the use of an adaptive, resource-efficient decision-making strategy is selectively downregulated in substance-related contexts. This study highlights the importance of considering contextual modulation and nuanced decision strategies in understanding habitual and goal-directed behavior in mental health conditions such as addiction.
